arbitrated.notes:
The five in-mandate drivers for the level call are inflation, labor_tightness, term_premium, financial_conditions, and balance_sheet. Inflation is the loudest and freshest signal: headline CPI yoy has rocketed from ~1% to 5.25%, core PCE to 3.93%, 3m-annualized core running 5.7%, and yoy_range_position at 0.99 (essentially a 12m high) — this is a clear, undeniable upside inflation impulse. Labor tightness confirms this from the other side: unemployment has fallen to a 12m low (5.4%), a full percentage point below its 6m level, sahm_gap positive — a tightening labor market, which is disinflationary-fighting/hawkish-for-yields. Term premium's own measurement (dgs10 level) has actually pulled back over 21d/63d (-0.21, -0.41pp) even though it's up over 252d — a stale-ish, recent cooling that partially offsets the inflation thrust, but the multi-month lookback still shows dgs10 elevated versus 12m lows and mid-range. Financial conditions (NFCI) are loosening only marginally (moving from -0.69 toward -0.66, still deeply negative = still loose), a mild disinflationary/curve-supportive signal but very low magnitude and somewhat stale-looking (flat for most of period, small recent uptick). Balance sheet is expanding steadily (+142.9B 4w, +5.66% 13w, near 52w high) — continued QE-style expansion is yield-suppressing (bearish for the "rises" framing of balance sheet's own measurement, which is expansion = growing, so conviction should be positive on assets rising, but this pushes yields down). 

Netting: strong inflation acceleration + tightening labor market are the dominant, freshest forces pushing nominal yields higher; growing balance sheet and mildly loosening financial conditions lean the other way but are of smaller and staler magnitude. The recent 21d/63d pullback in term premium tempers conviction. Overall a modest bullish-yield (higher) tilt, sized moderately given the offsetting balance-sheet/NFCI drag and the recent cooling in the term premium's own short-term measurement.
arbitrated.falsifier: A reversal in CPI/core PCE prints back toward 12m lows, or unemployment ticking back up, would flip this toward lower yields; also a fresh acceleration in NFCI loosening or QT resumption would offset.

risks.text: Term premium's own short-term pullback could presage broader yield declines if it persists.
Continued balance sheet expansion could suppress yields more than inflation/labor push them up.
Asset manager positioning is stretched (z near 2), risk of a mean-reversion rally in bonds (lower yields).

trade.rationale: Modest net-higher-yield level view driven by strong inflation acceleration and tightening labor market, tempered by balance sheet expansion and NFCI easing; symmetric long-duration-short (higher yield) tilt across both tenors.

why.inflation: CPI yoy and core PCE both near 12m highs, 3m annualized core at 5.7%; unambiguous fresh acceleration.
why.labor_tightness: Unemployment fell to 12m low 5.4%, sahm_gap positive; own measurement (unrate) clearly falling = tighter labor.
why.term_premium: dgs10 own level down 21d/63d despite 252d rise; recent cooling tempers the term-premium impulse.
why.financial_conditions: NFCI ticking up from -0.69 toward -0.66, small loosening trend but still deeply negative/stale-looking.
why.balance_sheet: Fed assets rising steadily, +5.66% 13w, near 52w high — clear expansion, own measurement rising.

arbitrated.notes:
This looks like the 2021 reflation/reopening episode: inflation running hot and accelerating (headline near 5.35% y/y, core PCE at 3.96% and rising, 3m annualized rates ~4.9-5%, breakevens grinding up to range highs), unemployment falling sharply and now at 12m lows (4.70%, sahm_gap positive, tightening labor market), a still-expanding Fed balance sheet (up ~4.8% over 13 weeks, at 52w highs — still adding accommodation, though the pace itself is what matters for direction of the stock, and the stock keeps growing which is disinflationary/duration-suppressing via more accommodation), and financial conditions that are easy and stable (NFCI near 52w lows, barely moving). Term premium proxy (DGS10) has been rising over the past year and last month, sitting near the top of its 12m range (range_position 0.79), consistent with rising nominal yields priced directly.

Synthesizing on the rate axis: hot and accelerating inflation pushes yields up; a tightening labor market (falling unemployment) pushes up via tighter policy expectations; easy financial conditions do not currently forecast tightening and are a mild offsetting force against a big yield rise but not enough to override the inflation/labor signal; balance sheet still expanding (assets rising) is accommodative and works against higher yields, creating a partial offset. The direct term-premium/DGS10 measurement itself confirms yields already trending higher over the past 21d and 252d. No stale-driver concerns here — all series look live and consistent. Net: yields biased higher, driven primarily by inflation and labor tightening, tempered slightly by an easy, expanding balance-sheet/financial-conditions backdrop. Conviction is moderate-high given directional consistency across independent series.
arbitrated.falsifier: A CPI/PCE print showing clear deceleration, or a jobs report showing unemployment ticking back up, would flip this toward a lower-yield read.

risks.text: Fed could accelerate taper/hike signals given hot inflation, amplifying the yield-up move beyond this read.
Balance sheet expansion could keep long-end anchored even as inflation and labor data push yields up.
Leveraged fund duration positioning shifting (z-scores rising) could exaggerate near-term yield moves either way.

trade.rationale: Net level view: hot inflation and tightening labor market outweigh easy financial conditions and expanding balance sheet, biasing both tenors' yields higher together.

why.financial_conditions: NFCI near 52w lows, flat/slightly easier, no tightening signal from this driver.
why.balance_sheet: Fed assets rising steadily, at 52w highs, +4.8% over 13w — balance sheet still expanding.
why.term_premium: DGS10 near top of 12m range, up over 21d/252d — direct evidence of rising long yields.

arbitrated.notes:
This panel is dominated by four in-scope drivers: inflation, labor tightness, term premium, financial conditions, and balance sheet (curve_slope, positioning, risk_appetite, sector_breadth, vol_regime are other pods' seats and not mine to weigh directly, though I note the broad risk-off tilt as context).

Inflation is unambiguous and fresh: headline CPI YoY has risen every print to 7.56%, core PCE to 5.36%, 3m annualized readings (8.95% headline, 6.65% core) running far above trend, and yoy_range_position sits at the top of its 12m range. This is a clear, live upside inflation signal.

Labor tightness: unemployment has fallen from 6.4% to 4.0%, near 12m lows, sahm_gap near zero — a clearly tightening labor market (falling unemployment = tighter labor, which is yield-supportive), though the latest tick up (3.9%→4.0%) is a small, likely noisy wobble.

Term premium: DGS10 sits near 12m highs (range_position 0.90), up 68bp over the year, with recent modest upward drift (21d +0.27pp) — consistent with rising term premium/yields.

Financial conditions (NFCI) are near the loose end of their 12m range (range_position 0.90) and roughly flat/tightening only marginally over 13w — not a strong offsetting force, mildly consistent with still-accommodative conditions that don't cap yields.

Balance sheet is expanding (+3.56% over 13w, near 52w highs), which is balance-sheet growth (my own-measurement conviction is positive per instructions), but expansion is disinflationary for term premium/duration supply dynamics — i.e., balance sheet growth pushes yields lower via increased official-sector demand, opposite in sign to its own-measurement direction.

Synthesis: inflation surging, labor tight, term premium drifting up — all point to higher nominal yields; only balance-sheet expansion is a modest offsetting force. Net view: yields higher, moderate-high conviction, one-month horizon steepening bias unclear (not my seat).

trade.rationale: Broad-based upward pressure on yields from surging inflation, tightening labor market, and rising term premium outweighs modest offset from balance-sheet expansion; symmetric duration-short bias across the curve.

arbitrated.notes:
Reading the five in-scope drivers (I set aside curve_slope, positioning, risk_appetite, sector_breadth, vol_regime, inflation_expectations as out-of-seat or supporting-only): inflation is running hot and accelerating — headline CPI yoy at 7.94%, up 1.04pp over 3m, with 3m-annualized headline at 8.25% and core at 6.65%, both far above the outgoing pace. This is a clear, fresh, high-conviction upside inflation signal. Labor market is tight and tightening further: unemployment at 3.90%, near the 12m low, sahm_gap near zero, distance-from-natural negative — a falling/low unemployment rate signals a tightening labor market, which is yield-positive. Financial conditions have eased noticeably (NFCI at range_position 1.00, rising 0.10 over 13w, less negative/less restrictive) — easier conditions support higher yields via reduced tightening pressure. Balance sheet is still expanding (assets_change_13w +246bn, +2.84%, at 52w high) — QE-style expansion, not QT, which is a factor pushing yields lower net of the other flows (expansion suppresses term premium/duration supply pressure). Term premium proxy (dgs10 level) has actually fallen recently (last print 1.83 vs prior ~1.97, 21d change only +0.02 but 63d/252d positive) — mixed, but the current level is off its highs, sitting at 74th percentile of 12m range, not screaming higher.

Net: inflation acceleration and a tightening labor market dominate, both clearly yield-positive and fresh. Easier financial conditions reinforce this. Balance sheet expansion is a mild offsetting force. Term premium read is inconclusive/stale relative to the other fresher signals. On balance I lean toward higher yields, with moderate-high conviction on the CPI/labor combination but tempered by the balance-sheet expansion and lack of strong term-premium confirmation.

This panel reads like the 2021-2022 tightening cycle in real time: inflation is accelerating hard (headline CPI 8.57% y/y, 3m annualized 10.1%, core PCE still rising to 5.6%), unemployment has fallen to 3.7% (a 12-month low, clearly tight labor), financial conditions are still easing/loose relative to their own 52w range (NFCI near its high end of the range, i.e. loosest, though the recent 4w/13w change is ticking up = tightening from an extreme), and the balance sheet is still expanding (assets at 52w highs, +2% over 13w) rather than shrinking. Term premium proxy (DGS10 level) sits near its 12m high with range position 0.88, having risen 46bp over 21 days and 80bp over 63 days — a live, non-stale, strongly rising signal. Curve is flattening sharply (2s10s compressing from 1.56pp high to 0.04pp), consistent with front-end repricing tightening expectations, which is a curve-shape signal I set aside per mandate but which corroborates the level story: yields have been rising fast, led by the front end but with the long end also climbing.

Synthesis for level: every driver I can read cleanly (inflation, labor tightness, term premium/DGS10 trend, and even the direction of balance-sheet policy) points to higher nominal yields. None of these look stale — they're all recent, multi-observation trends moving in the same direction. Financial conditions are the only mild complication: still loose in level terms but tightening at the margin, consistent with rising yields, not contradicting the call. I do not see a genuine disagreement across drivers here — this is a coherent tightening-cycle picture, so I take a confident but not maximal long-yield (short duration) stance, keeping some conviction in reserve given the sheer speed of the move (real-world curves like this can overshoot and mean-revert).

This is a 2022-style regime: inflation hot and re-accelerating (headline 3m annualized 8.8%, core 5.5%, both yoy still rising off 12m lows, yoy_range_position 0.91 near cycle highs), labor market historically tight (unemployment at 12-month and cycle low 3.7%, sahm_gap flat, distance from natural negative), financial conditions easing (NFCI at 52w-high position, i.e., loosest reading in the window, rising off lows), and the balance sheet still growing (assets_change_13w/52w firmly positive, near 52w high) — a modest QT-absence/expansion signal that is disinflationary for term premium but here read as its own metric rising. Term premium proxy (DGS10 level) is at 98th percentile of its 12m range, up sharply on 21/63/252d windows, confirming curveward pressure already realized. Inflation expectations (10y breakeven) are also grinding higher over 63d/252d, corroborating the inflation call rather than contradicting it — no gap here since both inflation and breakevens agree.

None of these drivers look stale — all are inside-month, fresh readings with consistent multi-window trends. There isn't a real split: inflation, labor tightness, term premium, financial-conditions-easing and balance-sheet growth all point the same direction — upward pressure on nominal yields. The only mild tension is balance sheet expansion itself (dovish in isolation) vs. everything else pushing yields up; but its own-measurement conviction (assets rising) is separate from the yield-direction synthesis, and its magnitude is small relative to the inflation/labor thrust.

Net: this panel supports higher nominal yields going into next month, driven by inflation momentum, tight labor, easier financial conditions, and already-realized upward momentum in the 10y level itself. I take a real but not maximal long-duration-short (yields up) position given the multi-driver agreement.

Labor: unemployment rate at 12m low (3.50%), still grinding down over 3/6/12m — a tightening labor market (falling unemployment). Financial conditions (NFCI) have tightened markedly off the 52w low, now at the 52w high and rising over 4w — conditions tightening, consistent with the rise in yields already reflected in the index. Balance sheet continues to run off (assets down 118k over 13w, near 52w low territory) — QT ongoing, a modest structural upward pressure on term premium/yields via supply-liquidity channel. All the fresh, live drivers here (term premium spike, NFCI tightening, ongoing QT, tight labor) point the same direction: upward pressure on nominal yield levels, partially offset only by cooling headline inflation momentum (though core sticky). Given multiple live, agreeing drivers and only one (partial) offsetting one, I lean toward higher yields, sized moderately given the disagreement between headline deceleration and core stickiness.

arbitrated.notes:
Reading the five in-scope drivers directly. Inflation: headline CPI yoy has cooled 0.7pp over 3m and sits off its 12m high, but core PCE yoy is still creeping up (+0.35pp over 3m) and both 3m-annualized headline (4.26%) and core (5.61%) run well above target — sticky, not collapsing. Net: mild upside lean on the inflation print itself given core's persistence, though headline is rolling over. Labor tightness: unemployment rate has ticked up slightly over 3m (+0.10pp) after a long downtrend (-0.90pp over 12m), sitting near cycle lows (3.60% vs 3.50% low) — the level is still historically tight but the trend has just inflected higher, a marginal loosening signal for the rate itself. Term premium proxy (DGS10 level): near 12m highs (range position 0.95), up sharply over 63d/252d, with only a modest pullback in the last print — momentum is still up. Financial conditions (NFCI): index has risen (loosened) steadily from -0.24 to -0.11, sitting near the loose end of its 52w range (range position 0.98) — conditions easing, which removes a headwind to growth/inflation and is consistent with yields staying supported. Balance sheet: assets falling on all horizons (4w, 13w) and near 52w lows — continued QT, a modest structural upward pressure on term premium/yields via supply, even though the driver's own measurement (assets) is declining.

Synthesizing: term premium momentum and easing financial conditions both point the same way (supportive of higher/stable yields), inflation is mixed (headline down, core still elevated) and labor is only very marginally loosening from tight levels. Balance sheet continues to shrink, adding a modest positive yield impulse. No driver here argues strongly for materially lower yields; conviction is moderate-to-modest for a mild upward yield tilt, tempered by the softer headline CPI trend.
arbitrated.falsifier: A sharp reversal in NFCI toward tightening, a renewed drop in DGS10 below its recent range, or a clear downside surprise in core PCE would flip this toward lower yields.

risks.text: Term premium proxy and financial conditions could reverse quickly if growth data disappoints.
Fed could pause or slow QT, removing the balance-sheet driven upward pressure on yields.
Extreme short positioning by leveraged funds could unwind, causing outsized yield moves either direction.

trade.rationale: Modest net upward tilt to yield level from firm term premium momentum, easing financial conditions, and ongoing QT, only partly offset by cooling headline inflation and slight labor loosening.

why.inflation: Headline CPI yoy cooling but core PCE yoy still rising 0.35pp/3m and 3m-annualized core at 5.6%; net mild upside lean.
why.labor_tightness: Unemployment rate off 12m lows, ticked up 0.10pp over 3m after long downtrend; marginal loosening from very tight base.
why.term_premium: DGS10 near 12m highs, up strongly over 63d/252d despite small recent pullback; momentum still up.
why.financial_conditions: NFCI risen steadily to near loose end of 52w range; conditions easing clearly over 4w/13w.
why.balance_sheet: Fed assets declining on 4w/13w basis, near 52w low; continued QT run-off.

arbitrated.notes:
Synthesizing the five in-scope drivers for level direction. Inflation: headline CPI YoY has fallen sharply (8.98% peak to 6.33%, -1.43pp over 3m), core PCE also declining though stickier (5.6%→4.94%, -0.52pp/3m); 3m annualized headline (3.28%) is well below the trailing yoy print, confirming a genuine disinflation trend. This is a clear, fresh, non-stale disinflation signal — pulls yields down. Labor tightness: unemployment sits at 3.5%, a 12-month low, flat-to-down over 3m/6m, sahm_gap near zero — labor market still tight, unrate falling to cycle lows is a tightening signal, which is yield-supportive (opposes the inflation pull). Term premium: DGS10 has fallen 31bp over 21d and 44bp over 63d, though it's still up 167bp over 252d and sits at the 71st percentile of its 12m range — recent momentum is downward, but starting from an elevated level. This is a live, fresh read favoring modestly lower yields near-term. Financial conditions: NFCI has eased steadily to -0.29, a 13-week low, in the loose half of its 52w range and still loosening (-0.08 over 4w) — looser financial conditions historically associate with less need for restrictive rates, a mild pull toward lower yields, though also reflects risk-on conditions that could keep term premium contained. Balance sheet: continued QT, assets down 253bn over 13w and 390bn over 52w, near 52w lows — shrinking balance sheet is a hawkish, yield-supportive (upward) force via reduced duration absorption, working against the other four.

Net: three of five drivers (inflation cooling, term premium falling, financial conditions loosening) point to lower yields; two (tight/tightening labor, ongoing QT) point higher. The inflation and term-premium reads are the freshest and most decisive in magnitude. I lean modestly lower in yields but size down given the split.

arbitrated.notes:
Synthesizing only the five in-scope drivers. Inflation: headline CPI YoY has fallen sharply (8.98%→3.07%, -1.85pp over 3m) and 3m annualized headline (2.94%) is near target, though core PCE YoY is stickier (4.73%, only -0.12pp over 3m) and core 3m annualized (3.97%) shows underlying persistence. Net trend is disinflationary but decelerating pace of decline — headline still falling, core roughly flat. I read this as inflation still drifting lower, clearly. Labor tightness: unemployment rate ticked up from a 3.40% low to 3.60%, sahm_gap positive (+0.13), range_position at top of 12m band — labor market loosening modestly, i.e. tightness easing (unemployment rising). Term premium: DGS10 up +0.17pp/21d, +0.33pp/63d, +0.61pp/252d, sitting at 73rd percentile of 12m range — clear uptrend in long yields, consistent with rising term premium demanded. Financial conditions: NFCI has been drifting more negative (looser) for 13 weeks, now at -0.22, near 52w low — conditions are easing/loosening, which is disinflationary for policy urgency but also signals less restrictive backdrop. Balance sheet: assets shrinking steadily (-4.19% over 13w, -572bn over 52w), clear ongoing QT — a falling balance sheet mechanically removes duration support and pressures yields up even though the "measurement" (assets) itself is falling.

Combining: falling inflation and loosening labor market argue for lower yields ahead, but rising term premium (DGS10 uptrend, near top of range) and continued balance-sheet runoff both argue for higher yields via duration supply/premium channels. Financial conditions loosening reduces the case for aggressive further hikes but doesn't cap term premium. On net, the live, fresher signals (term premium uptrend, ongoing QT) look more determinative for the level than the decelerating-but-lagged inflation print, giving a mild upward tilt to yields, tempered by disinflation and labor loosening.

arbitrated.notes:
Reading the five in-mandate drivers directly: inflation is decelerating — headline CPI yoy fell to 3.72% from an 8%+ peak with core 3m annualized at just 2.05% and core yoy down 0.90pp in three months; that's a clean disinflation signal, not stale. Labor tightness is loosening at the margin — unemployment rate ticked up to 3.70%, a 12-month high, with a positive sahm_gap and unrate at the top of its range; this is a cooling labor market (own-measurement rises, but that means looser, not tighter, labor). Financial conditions (NFCI) are easing further into negative territory, now at a 52-week low (-0.32), falling for 13 straight weeks — looser financial conditions, own measurement falls. Balance sheet continues to shrink steadily (-104bn 4w, -297bn 13w, -712bn 52w, currently 693bn below 52w high) — still an active QT drag, own measurement (assets) falls, which is a hawkish/higher-yield force via reduced duration absorption. Term premium proxy (DGS10 level) has been rising over the medium term (+0.48pp 63d, +0.97pp 252d) even as it's flat to slightly down over 21d, sitting in the 80th percentile of its 12-month range — suggesting an elevated and persistent term premium.

Netting these: two disinflationary/dovish forces (inflation cooling, labor loosening) plus easier financial conditions argue for lower yields, but they are partially offset by continued balance-sheet runoff (structurally supportive of higher term premium) and a term premium measure sitting near cycle highs and still climbing on a multi-month basis. The panel is not unanimous — disinflation and softening labor point down, term premium and balance sheet point up — so I size the level view moderately rather than aggressively, tilting modestly toward lower yields given the strength and freshness of the inflation and labor readings versus the slower-moving balance sheet/term premium signals.

arbitrated.notes:
Reading only the drivers relevant to the level of nominal yields (inflation, labor tightness, term premium, financial conditions, balance sheet), the picture is one of moderate upward pressure on yields with some cross-currents. Inflation: headline CPI yoy is roughly flat over 3m (-0.04pp) but core PCE yoy has decelerated meaningfully (-0.83pp over 3m) and 3m-annualized core (2.31%) is well below the 12m trend — disinflation continuing, own-measurement direction is down. Labor tightness: unemployment rate has risen from 3.4% to 3.9%, a clear uptrend (+0.4pp 3m, +0.5pp 6m), sahm_gap positive — labor market loosening (unemployment rising), which is disinflationary/dovish for yields even though the driver's own headline measurement (unemployment rate) is rising. Term premium: DGS10 has risen steadily, +0.29pp over 21d, +0.83pp over 63d, sitting near 12m highs (range position 0.94) — clear upward momentum, live and fresh signal. Financial conditions: NFCI is near 52w lows (loose conditions), slight uptick over 4w (+0.04) but still easy — supportive of higher yields on the margin (less need for Fed support), a mild lean toward tighter/higher. Balance sheet: continued runoff, accelerating even (-94234 over 4w, -335514 over 13w), a clear ongoing QT signal — shrinking balance sheet is yield-supportive (reduced demand/duration absorption), even though its own measurement (assets) is falling.

Netting these: term premium is the freshest, most unambiguous upward force on yields and dominates. Balance sheet runoff reinforces upward pressure. Loosening labor market and decelerating core inflation are disinflationary and argue for lower yields, creating a genuine split on the level. Given the split, I size moderately rather than aggressively, leaning modestly higher on yields given the term premium's directness and QT's persistence outweigh the labor/inflation cooling for near-term Treasury yield levels.

arbitrated.notes:
Synthesizing the five level-relevant drivers I have a mandate on: inflation is cooling clearly (headline and core CPI/PCE yoy both down 3m, 3m-annualized core at 2.31% vs distance-from-target still 1.47pp but trending down fast, disinflation intact) — this argues for lower yields. Labor tightness: unemployment has drifted up from 3.4 low to 3.7-3.9, sahm_gap positive and rising, unrate_3m_avg above 12m low — labor market loosening, which is disinflationary/growth-negative and pulls yields down too (a loosening labor market is lower tightness, supportive of lower yields). Financial conditions (NFCI) are near 52w lows and have eased over 13w (small +0.02 rise off very loose levels, but 4w still easing at -0.02) — conditions remain accommodative/loose, which is a modest offsetting force keeping yields from falling as much, but the signal is weak and range_position is only 0.16 (near loose end), so this is a modest counterweight, not dominant. Term premium: DGS10 has bounced off recent lows (4.27 trough to 4.37), 63d change +0.25pp and 252d +0.62pp show rising term premium pressure — a genuine offsetting force pushing yields higher, consistent with term-premium re-steepening seen in curve data. Balance sheet: still shrinking (QT ongoing), 4w/13w/52w all firmly negative — a shrinking balance sheet is a hawkish/higher-yield force via reduced duration absorption, another offset to the disinflation/labor-loosening pull down.

Net: two forces (inflation cooling, labor loosening) pull yields down; two forces (rising term premium, ongoing balance sheet runoff) push yields up; financial conditions are loose but only mildly directional. This is a genuinely mixed panel — I lean modestly toward lower yields on the back of the clearer, fresher disinflation and labor-loosening signals, but size down given the real offsetting pressure from term premium and QT continuation.

arbitrated.notes:
The five in-mandate drivers for the level call are inflation, labor_tightness, term_premium, financial_conditions, and balance_sheet. Inflation is clearly disinflating: headline and core CPI/PCE y/y are both falling with 3m annualized core near 1.8%, well below the trailing 12m trend, and breakevens are drifting down too — a disinflation impulse that argues for lower yields. Labor tightness is loosening at the margin: unemployment has risen from a 3.4% low to 3.8%, a 0.3-0.4pp climb over 6-12m sitting near the top of its 12m range — looser labor is disinflationary/dovish and also pulls yields down. Term premium, read through DGS10's own behavior, has fallen materially (-39bp over 21d, -71bp over 63d) and sits only in the 35th percentile of its 12m range — a compressing risk premium/duration term that is consistent with, and probably reflects, the same forces pulling yields down. Financial conditions (NFCI) have eased further into more accommodative territory, at a 52w low, which on the margin removes a tightening force but is a second-order input to yields versus growth/inflation. Balance sheet continues to run off (-3.6% over 13w, -838bn y/y) which is a genuine hawkish/higher-yield offset via reduced duration absorption, but it's a slower-moving, structural drag rather than a swing factor month to month, and its pace hasn't accelerated.

Netting these: three high-conviction, undeniably fresh drivers (inflation cooling, labor loosening, term premium compressing) all point toward lower yields, while only balance sheet runoff argues the other way, and that runoff is unchanged in pace. The panel is not split — it's aligned on the yields-down side with one structural offset. I have no view on curve shape or real/nominal split, only the level, so I lean toward a modest bullish-duration (yields lower) tilt sized down by the balance sheet drag and by the inherent noise in one-month-ahead CPI/labor surprises.

trade.rationale: Aligned disinflation, loosening labor, and compressing term premium outweigh steady balance-sheet runoff; modest duration-long (yields lower) across both tenors, sized down for one offsetting driver.

arbitrated.notes:
Synthesizing the five in-scope rate drivers (inflation, labor tightness, term premium, financial conditions, balance sheet) into a single nominal-yield level view. Inflation: headline CPI yoy is flat-to-slightly-up over 3m (+0.02pp) while core PCE yoy continues to decelerate (-0.32pp over 3m) and 3m-annualized core (3.29%) sits below the 12m trend — net a mild disinflationary drift, still ~1.2pp above target, so no strong directional pull on yields from this axis. Labor tightness: unemployment rate has risen steadily (+0.2pp/3m, +0.3pp/12m, sitting at 12m-high, Sahm gap +0.4pp) — clear loosening of labor market, historically yield-negative (dovish) as growth/inflation risk fades. Term premium: dgs10 has drifted up over 21d (+0.19) but is flat-to-down over 63d and 252d shows the larger up move (+0.33); level is mid-range (0.57 position) — a modestly firm but not clearly rising term premium signal. Financial conditions: NFCI is at its 52-week low and still loosening (-0.03 over 4w, -0.11 over 13w) — looser conditions typically associated with less need for restrictive yields, modest downward pull. Balance sheet: still shrinking briskly (-95.5B in 4w, -229B in 13w, near 52w lows) — continued QT is a persistent upward pressure on term premium/yields via supply effects, even though the "measurement" (assets) itself is falling.

Net: labor loosening and loose financial conditions both lean toward lower yields; ongoing balance-sheet runoff leans yields higher; inflation is roughly neutral/mixed. These are offsetting-but-tilted-lower forces — the labor deterioration is the freshest, most unambiguous signal, while term premium is only mildly firm. I read the net level view as modestly biased toward lower yields, sized moderately given the multi-driver split.

{"notes": "Synthesizing the five in-scope rate-axis drivers (inflation, labor tightness, term premium, financial conditions, balance sheet), the level case for yields is modestly higher, but with meaningful offsets that argue for sizing down rather than a high-conviction directional bet.

Inflation: headline CPI yoy has ticked up the last two prints (3.16→3.49) with 3m annualized headline running hot at 4.75% versus a 12m low of 3.07%, though core PCE yoy continues to grind lower (3m annualized 4.78% is stale relative to yoy trend which is flat-to-down). Net: inflation's own measurement is turning up at the margin, a modest upside conviction on inflation itself, which pushes yields higher.

Labor tightness: unemployment rate has drifted up from 3.40% low to 3.90%, sahm_gap positive at 0.43pp, rate sitting at 12m high. This is a labor market own-measurement rise (looser labor), which is yield-negative (inverted read) — but the direction of unemployment itself is clearly rising.

Term premium: DGS10 has fallen slightly over 21d (-0.07pp) but risen substantially over 63d (+0.41pp) and 252d (+0.65pp), sitting near the middle of its 12m range (0.54). The near-term drift is flat-to-down, but medium-term momentum argues term premium is not collapsing — a mild higher lean.

Financial conditions: NFCI continues to loosen (more negative, -0.43, at 52w low), a slow steady loosening trend — this is disinflationary/growth-supportive, modestly yield-negative from a tightening-conditions perspective, but the loosening itself is the own-measurement direction (index falling).

Synthesizing the five in-scope rate drivers (inflation, labor_tightness, term_premium, financial_conditions, balance_sheet), the net pull on nominal yield levels is mildly higher, though the panel is not unanimous and several reads are stale or slow-moving.

Inflation: core PCE yoy has decelerated steadily (4.73→2.77 over 13mo, -0.29pp over 3m) and 3m-annualized core/headline are both near/at target (2.81%/2.87%). This is a clear disinflationary trend, arguing for lower yields via reduced inflation risk. Headline yoy is noisier and ticked up recently but the trend and 3m-annualized measures dominate.

Labor: unemployment has drifted up from a 3.50 low to 3.90, near its 12m high, sahm_gap +0.40pp — a loosening labor market (own measurement rising). A loosening labor market is disinflationary/growth-negative, consistent with downward yield pressure, though the level (3.9%) is still low historically.

Term premium: DGS10 has been rising 21d(-0.12 partial reversal) but 63d/252d changes are firmly positive (+0.32/+0.82pp), sitting at 66th percentile of 12m range. This is the freshest, most directly rate-relevant driver and shows underlying upward term premium/level pressure over the medium term, only recently stalling.

Financial conditions: NFCI is flat-to-slightly-tightening at the margin (-0.43→-0.41, near top of 52w range), a modest but stale/slow-moving signal, tilting mildly toward easier conditions supporting slightly lower yields, weak signal.

Balance sheet: Fed assets continue to shrink (QT ongoing, -3.75% 13w, -1.1M 52w), a persistent contractionary force that structurally pushes yields higher via reduced duration absorption — this argues for higher yields even as the balance sheet itself falls (inverse relationship).

Net: disinflation and labor loosening pull yields down; continued QT and elevated realized term premium trend pull yields up. These roughly offset, with a slight net tilt toward modestly higher yields given the freshness and directness of the term-premium/QT signals versus the slower-moving inflation/labor trends. I hold a small, low-conviction long-duration-yield (short bonds) tilt.

arbitrated.notes:
Synthesizing the five rate-relevant drivers I have a mandate over. Inflation: headline CPI yoy has fallen to 2.97% (12m low) with 3m annualized headline at just 0.90% and core 3m annualized at 2.81%, both decelerating clearly from a year ago — disinflation is live and fresh (last print negative m/m). This argues for lower yields via the inflation channel. Labor tightness: unemployment has risen steadily to 4.10%, a 12m high, with positive change over 3/6/12m and a Sahm gap of +0.47pp — labor market is loosening (less tight), which is disinflationary/dovish for policy and pulls yields down. Term premium: DGS10 sits at 4.36, near the middle of its 12m range (range_position 0.51) but has ticked up over 21d (-0.25 actually, wait: dgs10_change_21d is -0.25pp, i.e., yields fell over the last month) while up over 63d/252d — so recent momentum is downward even as the longer trend has been up; this is a mixed/stale-ish signal, I weight the more recent -0.25pp move higher. Financial conditions: NFCI is near a 52w low, slightly easing (less tight) over 4w/13w, in the loose portion of its range — modestly consistent with easier conditions, which alone doesn't directly push yields but reduces the case for higher term premium. Balance sheet: assets continue to shrink (-53B 4w, -253B 13w, -3.39% 13w change), a clear ongoing runoff — QT continues, a mechanical upward pressure on yields via reduced Fed absorption of duration, but the direction of the driver itself (assets) is falling clearly.

Net picture: three of four rate-relevant fundamental drivers (inflation, labor tightness, term premium momentum) point toward lower yields, while balance-sheet runoff pushes the other way structurally but is a slower-moving, well-priced force. Financial conditions are neutral-to-slightly-easing. On balance, I lean toward modestly lower yields, sized down given the mixed balance-sheet signal and only middling term-premium clarity.

Term premium's longer-run trend (63d/252d) is still rising, contradicting the recent 21d dip I weighted.
Leveraged funds and asset managers show volatile positioning shifts that could amplify moves either direction.

trade.rationale: Disinflation and labor loosening dominate over ongoing but well-anticipated QT; modest duration-long (lower yields) position sized down given mixed term-premium signal.

Financial conditions: NFCI has been drifting up (loosening less negative) from -0.41 to -0.36, a mild tightening in financial conditions register wise — index rising signals conditions tightening slightly, though still well below zero (accommodative territory) and range position mid-pack. Balance sheet: assets continue to shrink (QT ongoing), 4w/13w/52w changes all negative, clearly falling — a shrinking balance sheet is yield-supportive (opposite sign to its own measurement, which I report as falling significantly).

Synthesizing: disinflation (yields down), rising unemployment/loosening labor (yields down), declining nominal 10y level directly observed (yields down), mild NFCI increase (slight tightening, modest yield-up pressure but small), and continued QT (mildly yield-up via term premium/supply channel, opposing lower yields). The dominant, freshest signals (inflation cooling, labor loosening, and directly observed lower nominal yields) all point the same direction — lower yields — outweighing the modest offsetting pressure from continued balance-sheet runoff and slightly firmer financial conditions. Conviction is moderate-high given multiple corroborating fresh series.

Financial conditions easing (looser, not tighter) removes a restraining force on growth/inflation, modestly yield-supportive. Balance sheet runoff continuing removes duration-absorption support (bearish for yields, i.e., pushes yields up via reduced Fed demand/QT effect) despite the metric itself falling. Inflation's own softening headline is yield-negative but core stickiness caps that. Net: modest upward bias to yields led by term premium and continued QT, tempered by loosening labor and financial conditions — a low-conviction, modestly long-yield (short duration) stance.

Labor_tightness: unemployment rate is at its 12m high (4.20%), up 0.5pp over 12m and flat over 3m at an elevated plateau. Sahm gap positive. Rising unemployment = looser labor market, which is disinflationary/growth-negative and argues for lower yields — this pulls against the inflation signal.

Term_premium: DGS10 has fallen from 4.43 to 4.18, a clear downtrend over 21d and 12m, sitting mid-range (0.51 range position) but decisively lower recently. This directly signals nominal yields declining — a strong, fresh, own-measurement read.

Financial_conditions: NFCI at 52-week low and still falling (-0.47, change -0.03 over 4w) — conditions are easing/loosening, consistent with lower risk premia and generally lower yield pressure, corroborating the term_premium downtrend.

Reading the five in-scope drivers (inflation, labor_tightness, term_premium, financial_conditions, balance_sheet) for a net level call on nominal yields, roughly one month out.

Inflation: headline CPI yoy has bounced off its 12m low (2.43→2.72) and 3m annualized readings (headline 3.18%, core 3.03%) sit above the recent yoy prints, with core yoy up 0.18pp over 3m. Labor_tightness: unemployment rate is at its 12m high (4.20%), up 0.5pp over 12m and flat over 3m at an elevated plateau. Sahm gap positive. Rising unemployment = looser labor market, which is disinflationary/growth-negative and argues for lower yields — this pulls against the inflation signal.

Term_premium: DGS10 has fallen from 4.43 to 4.18, a clear downtrend over 21d and 12m, sitting mid-range (0.51 range position) but decisively lower recently. This directly signals nominal yields declining — a strong, fresh, own-measurement read.

Financial_conditions: NFCI at 52-week low and still falling (-0.47, change -0.03 over 4w) — conditions are easing/loosening, consistent with lower risk premia and generally lower yield pressure, corroborating the term_premium downtrend.

Balance_sheet: Fed assets still shrinking (QT continuing), down 218bn over 13w, accelerating pace (4w change -108bn is roughly double the 13w/13 pace) — this is a persistent drainage that mechanically supports higher term premium/yields (shrinking balance sheet pushes yields up), an offset to the other three.

Net: term_premium and financial_conditions (both fresh, actual yield-level data) point down; balance_sheet is a persistent modest upward offset; inflation modestly up; labor loosening pulls down. The actual yield-level readings (DGS10 falling, easing NFCI) are the most directly informative and freshest, so I lean toward a modest downward drift in yields, tempered by continued QT and firming inflation prints — hence a small, low-conviction net-lower stance rather than a strong directional call.

Reading only the drivers within my mandate (inflation, labor tightness, term premium, financial conditions, balance sheet), the net signal is modestly higher yields, but with real disagreement in magnitude.

Inflation: headline CPI YoY has troughed and is reaccelerating (2.43% low back up to 2.87%, 3m annualized 3.70% vs 12m target distance still +0.99pp on core). Breakevens also drifting up (+0.19pp over 63d, range position 0.78). This is a live, non-stale upturn — leans yields higher.

Term premium: DGS10 has climbed steadily, near top of 12m range (0.89 position), sustained uptrend over 21d/63d/252d — this is a clear, live rise in term premium/level, directly supportive of higher yields, and is the freshest, cleanest signal here.

Financial conditions: NFCI at 52w low, still loosening (change_4w -0.01, change_13w -0.06) — easy financial conditions, own index falling, which means conditions are easing, consistent with less restrictive backdrop, mildly yield-supportive but modest.

Balance sheet: assets shrinking steadily (4w, 13w, 52w all firmly negative, near 52w low) — continued QT, which is disinflationary for reserves but mechanically supports higher term premium/yields via reduced duration absorption.

Net: term premium and reaccelerating inflation dominate and point toward higher yields; balance sheet runoff reinforces upward pressure; labor loosening is a modest offset. I lean moderately higher yields, not maximal conviction given the labor offset and mixed financial conditions.

Term premium proxy (DGS10 level) has fallen further: -0.19pp over 21d, essentially flat over 63d/252d, sitting mid-range (0.53 position) — recent momentum is down. Financial conditions (NFCI) are loosening steadily: -0.03 over 4w, -0.06 over 13w, now at -0.49, near the 52w low — easier conditions historically associate with less upward yield pressure from risk premia, and directionally the index itself is falling. Balance sheet continues to shrink (QT ongoing): -11bn 4w, -78bn 13w, -569bn over 52w, still well below the 52w high — clear ongoing contraction, which is yield-supportive on its own (less duration absorption capacity) but here we just note its own measurement is falling.

Synthesizing: inflation trend is softening, term premium/DGS10 has downward momentum, financial conditions are easing (bullish for duration/lower yields), while balance sheet contraction is a persistent hawkish counterweight and labor market is roughly neutral. On net, most live, non-stale signals point toward modestly lower yields — I lean short-duration-yield exposure (higher price / lower yield) with moderate conviction, sized down given the balance-sheet drag and mixed labor read.

arbitrated.notes:
Reading only the drivers I'm mandated to weigh in on: inflation, labor tightness, term premium, financial conditions, and balance sheet. Inflation is the clearest signal: headline CPI YoY has risen sharply into the newest print (3.02%, top of 12m range), core PCE ticking up too, and 3m annualized headline (3.54%) running above trailing YoY — this is a live, fresh, unambiguous upside surprise in inflation that pushes yields higher. Labor tightness: unemployment rate has climbed to 4.40%, a 12m high, up 0.30pp over 3m and 12m — a rising unemployment rate signals a loosening labor market, which is disinflationary/dovish and pulls yields lower, partially offsetting the inflation signal. Term premium: DGS10 itself is little changed on net — down slightly over 21d/63d but up over 252d, sitting mid-range (0.40 range position) — a stale, directionless read, so I give it little weight standalone. Financial conditions (NFCI) are flat at multi-year lows (-0.52, barely moving over 4w/13w) — very easy conditions, marginally easing further, which is consistent with some room for yields to grind higher without tightening feedback, but the signal is weak/stale given near-zero recent change. Balance sheet: assets fell over 13w and 52w but ticked up over the most recent 4w (+5011) — a mixed, recently-stabilizing runoff, mildly hawkish (less accommodation) but not a strong active signal this month.

Netting these: the inflation upside is the freshest and strongest force, partially countered by a genuinely loosening labor market (higher unemployment). Financial conditions and balance sheet are weak/stale and don't materially move the level. On balance I lean mildly higher yields, driven primarily by the inflation reacceleration, tempered by softening labor and directionless term premium — modest conviction, not a strong call.

{"notes": "Synthesizing the five rate-relevant drivers I'm mandated to judge (inflation, labor_tightness, term_premium, financial_conditions, balance_sheet), the picture is one of modest, low-conviction pressure toward slightly lower yields, with meaningful internal disagreement that argues for a small position rather than a strong directional bet.

Inflation: headline CPI yoy has re-accelerated from a 2.33 trough to 3.02, with 3m annualized headline running hot at 3.54%, well above core PCE's 2.60% annualized and above target-distance readings. This is a genuine upside inflation impulse, though core PCE yoy is actually drifting down slightly. Net: mixed-to-firmer headline momentum, leaning up.

Labor tightness: unemployment has climbed steadily from 4.00 to 4.40, a clear multi-month deterioration (12m range position at max, Sahm gap positive). Rising unemployment = weaker labor market = tighter labor tightness measure falls, which is disinflationary/dovish for yields.

Term premium: DGS10 is range-bound near recent lows (range position 0.17, near 12m low), with 21d/63d/252d changes all negative or flat — no evidence of rising term premium; if anything modest compression given yields have consolidated after last year's higher levels.

Financial conditions: NFCI is stable and slightly loosening (near 52w low, flat to marginally less negative) — not signaling stress that would compress yields via flight-to-quality, mild support for higher yields on lack of tightening.

Synthesizing the five rate-relevant drivers I'm mandated to judge (inflation, labor_tightness, term_premium, financial_conditions, balance_sheet), the picture is one of modest, low-conviction pressure toward slightly lower yields, with meaningful internal disagreement that argues for a small position rather than a strong directional bet.

Inflation: headline CPI yoy has re-accelerated from a 2.33 trough to 3.02, with 3m annualized headline running hot at 3.54%, well above core PCE's 2.60% annualized and above target-distance readings. This is a genuine upside inflation impulse, though core PCE yoy is actually drifting down slightly. Net: mixed-to-firmer headline momentum, leaning up.

Labor tightness: unemployment has climbed steadily from 4.00 to 4.40, a clear multi-month deterioration (12m range position at max, Sahm gap positive). Rising unemployment = weaker labor market = tighter labor tightness measure falls, which is disinflationary/dovish for yields.

Term premium: DGS10 is range-bound near recent lows (range position 0.17, near 12m low), with 21d/63d/252d changes all negative or flat — no evidence of rising term premium; if anything modest compression given yields have consolidated after last year's higher levels.

Financial conditions: NFCI is stable and slightly loosening (near 52w low, flat to marginally less negative) — not signaling stress that would compress yields via flight-to-quality, mild support for higher yields on lack of tightening.

Balance sheet: still shrinking steadily (assets down ~55.5bn over 13w, near cycle lows vs 52w high), continued QT — mechanically balance-sheet-driven term premium/duration supply pressure remains a modest upward force on yields, though the pace of decline (4w change ~flat) suggests QT is decelerating.

Net: rising unemployment and stable-to-lower term premium outweigh the inflation upturn and continued (but slowing) QT. This argues for a mild bias toward lower yields, sized small given cross-currents.

arbitrated.notes:
Reading the five in-scope drivers directly: Inflation (headline CPI yoy) is near 12-month highs (2.99%, range position 0.95) with 3m annualized headline at 3.64%, though core PCE has cooled slightly and breakevens are drifting down. Net: headline inflation is running hot and rising, a modest upward pull on nominal yields, but the breakeven-implied expectations component is softening, tempering the read. Labor tightness: unemployment rate has climbed steadily to 4.50%, a 12-month high, sahm_gap positive and rising — this is a clear loosening in labor market (falling tightness), which is disinflationary and yield-negative on the growth/labor channel. Term premium: DGS10 has fallen from 4.14 to 4.02, a clear downtrend over 21d/63d/252d, sitting near 12-month lows (range position 0.06) — this directly signals lower long-end yields, a fresh and strong read. Financial conditions: NFCI is easing very modestly (slightly less negative), still deeply accommodative and near 52w lows, marginal loosening bias, weak signal. Balance sheet: Fed assets continue to shrink (QT ongoing), 4w/13w/52w all negative, consistent with continued runoff — this is yield-supportive (less demand for duration from Fed) but a slow, well-priced grind.

Weighing these: term premium gives the freshest, clearest directional signal — nominal 10y yields are actively falling and near cycle lows. Labor tightness confirms the labor market is loosening, consistent with disinflationary growth backdrop supporting lower yields. Inflation is hot on trailing prints but expectations are softening, a genuine split reducing conviction on the inflation channel. Financial conditions are stale/marginal. Balance sheet is a slow structural upward pull but overwhelmed by the flight to duration evident in term premium data. Net level view: modest downward drift in nominal yields, driven mainly by falling term premium and loosening labor market, partially offset by sticky headline inflation.
arbitrated.falsifier: A rebound in DGS10 back toward 4.10-4.15 alongside sticky breakevens, or unemployment reversing back below 4.2%, would flip this to a level-up call.

Hot headline CPI could force a hawkish repricing that overrides labor-market softening.
Leveraged fund positioning shows large short covering, which could amplify yield moves either direction.

trade.rationale: Net level view is modestly lower yields, driven by falling term premium and loosening labor market, partially offset by sticky inflation; sizing down given cross-driver split.

arbitrated.notes:
Reading only the five drivers in my remit. Inflation is the standout: headline CPI YoY has surged from 2.66 to 4.27 over three prints, 3m annualized headline is running 8.2%, core PCE also drifting up to 3.41% and away from target. This is fresh, unambiguous, and points to inflation clearly rising — a strong upward pressure on nominal yields. Labor tightness is more mixed/stale-ish: unemployment rate at 4.30%, flat over 3 months, sahm gap modest, range position at midpoint — no clear directional move, effectively a wash, marginal loosening bias (12m change +0.10pp) but noisy. Financial conditions (NFCI) are stable-to-slightly-easier, sitting near 13w average, index still deeply negative (easy conditions), not tightening — this argues against needing higher term premium compensation from a risk-off angle, mild dovish-for-yields signal but essentially flat. Balance sheet: assets have been grinding higher over 4w/13w/52w windows (+1.18% 13w, near 52w high) — this is not a shrinking balance sheet, it's expanding modestly, which should be viewed as balance sheet growing (headline measurement rising), a mild QT-pause/reflation signal that is technically yield-supportive via more liquidity but per instructions I report own-direction only. Term premium proxy (DGS10 level) has been rangebound, 21d down -0.15pp, 63d up +0.08pp, sitting mid-upper part of 12m range — no strong trend, near-term dip.

Netting these: inflation is the loudest and freshest signal, clearly rising, which dominates the level call and argues for higher nominal yields. Labor tightness and financial conditions are flat/inconclusive, providing no offsetting force. Balance sheet expansion is a secondary supportive-for-duration-price (yield-suppressing) factor but modest. Term premium data show no strong independent trend. Net: modest bearish (higher yield) duration view, driven primarily by inflation acceleration, tempered by absence of confirmation elsewhere.
